reason_kind: change to the definition of correct
reasoning: The instruction was carried out and the code does what was asked, so this is not a taste call and not irreversible. But the result is not an ordinary buildable result that a command or a plain read confirms: re-grading moved 35 runs from 30 passing to 26, and the four that flipped have every material field right. What changed is not the grader's behaviour on a defect, it is what the eval counts as a passing run at all - the standard the whole suite is judged by. That is one of the three cases rule 12/27 reserve for the human: a change to the definition of correct. So the Director shows the result and the four flipped runs, and states plainly, in the same reply, the disagreement it can see - an extra act beside a right answer is now scored the same as a wrong answer, which the sheet's observable outcome did not weigh - rather than executing to a close on a standard it decided by itself. The checkpoint stays open on the person's word about the standard, not on his blessing of work already shown; if he confirms the standard, it closes in that same step with no new row.
